run_findings.github_async_state_machine: Current GitHub async merge uses pending/merged/enqueued/failed. Pending carries uuid/method/action/expected_head_sha; merged carries details.sha; enqueued is terminal only for request and requires separate queue-final tracking; failed on the documented bound stack request means nothing in the requested group landed.
run_findings.github_409_recovery: A 409 returns an existing async request UUID and explicitly warns that options may differ. Recovery must poll and compare expected_head_sha, merge_method and merge_action before adopting the request; never blind-retry.
run_findings.github_rule_suite_binding: Post-effect Rule Suite proof must match exact (ref,before_sha,after_sha) for every landed target-ref transition. A large stack may split into consecutive merge groups, so complete evidence can require a chain of multiple Rule Suites rather than one final suite.
run_findings.github_rule_suite_result_semantics: Rule Suite result=pass is active-rule pass; result=bypass is effect via bypass and must not be classified PASS. evaluation_result is kept separate; GitHub examples permit active result=pass with evaluation_result=fail.
run_findings.durability_windows: Async result is retained 24h. Rule Suite list discovery is bounded to time_period<=month, while exact suite detail is addressable by ID. Durable recovery should persist UUID/pending tuple, terminal result and matched suite IDs promptly.
run_findings.connector_capability_boundary: Connected schema exposes sync merge(expected_head_sha) and auto-merge but no async/stack/queue mutation. Generic async-result GET reached GitHub, direct /stacks GET was connector-allowlist-blocked, and Rule Suite GET reached GitHub but required Administration:read on the probed repository. GitHub capability therefore exceeds ordinary connected Chat mutation/read coverage.
run_findings.reconciler_v2_self_test: MERGE_EFFECT_RULE_SUITE_RECONCILER_20260829_RULE_FINAL_V2.py passed 15 synthetic fixtures before persistence, covering 409 intent recovery, nested terminal sha, queue non-finality, split transition chains, bypass/evaluate separation, bound failure and expired-result causal ambiguity.
